language: Python 3.11+ (CI runs 3.14.8); adapters drive Python and Node.js projects
summary: recipes turns the typed targets in a repo's manifest into concrete actions, with one adapter per target kind found by a single loader. It is the only place in qq allowed to name a language, build tool or test runner, which keeps the rest of the system language-agnostic.

how_it_works.title: Kinds map to adapter modules
how_it_works.text: loader.load(kind) imports qqrecipes.adapters.<kind with - replaced by _> and returns its ADAPTER, so adding a kind is adding a module. A missing module is AdapterNotFound, while an adapter that fails to import raises so a broken install never looks like a missing kind.

how_it_works.title: Capabilities produce actions
how_it_works.text: An adapter implements some of fetch, build, test, package, run, deploy, bench and fuzz, and an unimplemented one is a declared state rather than an error. Each capability returns REAPI-shaped actions: a command, an input root digest, environment, outputs and toolchain pins.

how_it_works.title: A digest is the cache key
how_it_works.text: Action.digest() covers the command, inputs, environment, outputs, toolchain pins, platform and a fingerprint of the recipes code. Commands use placeholders like {toolchain:NAME} and {out} that the runner resolves, so the key is the same on every machine of a platform.

how_it_works.title: Every step leaves JUnit
how_it_works.text: The v0 runner executes each action as a subprocess on this machine. A step that writes no JUnit XML of its own, such as a typecheck, gets a one-case report from its exit code.

key_files.what: Adapter base class, Target, Context and the REAPI-shaped Action.

status.text: Three adapters exist: python-service, pytest and node-app. All five v0 items (contract and loader, Python adapters, node-app, property tests, canary deploy) are marked merged.
This all runs in recipes' own presubmit, not yet in the gate. xo-space and innernet are checked out at pinned commits and read through sync's fixture manifests rather than their own.
In presubmit, toolchains come from GitHub's setup actions at the pinned versions, not yet from quirq-ai/toolchains.
Deploy's only backend in v0 is local: on GitHub that is the Actions runner, where the service is started, probed and always torn down.
